coordination.reason: The active WP105 lane owns canonical mutation. This record only corrects contradictory review evidence and identifies the next integration discriminator.

correction.epistemic_note: The later review omitted an already-present current-authority binding surface. Its historical-donor nonpromotion concern was valid before explicit re-entry, but the binding record itself supplies that exact re-entry without creating a second authority.

observed_effect_gate_semantics: EffectGate.execute then calls EffectJournal.begin, creating canonical PENDING before the action.
The same EffectGate.execute call then performs state.noop or EntityOSBridge.run itself and finalizes the journal VERIFIED/DENIED/FAILED before returning.
EffectJournal.recover_pending converts residual PENDING rows to UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART and never authorizes blind replay.
observed_f2_semantics: CanonicalEffectAuthorityPort is currently modeled as an authorization call returning PENDING evidence before a separate F2 executor dispatch.
dispatch_with_canonical_authority therefore assumes the authority call itself has not already executed the real effect.
new_blocker.contradiction: Calling the bound EffectGate.execute as CanonicalEffectAuthorityPort would execute and finalize the effect during the supposed authorization phase, after which the F2 executor path would risk a second dispatch. Calling EffectJournal.begin directly would avoid that double-dispatch but bypass EffectGate policy/replay/lease checks and therefore cannot be treated as canonical authorization.
new_blocker.additional_lease_constraint: For entityos.exec the bound EffectGate acquires and releases its automatic lease inside execute(). Splitting authorization and execution across an external executor would require a new canonical lease-bearing protocol rather than an F2-local workaround.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Reuse EffectJournal.begin directly as the production pre-dispatch authority adapter.
counterhypotheses.reason: It journals identity but does not perform the full EffectGate capability/session/generation/replay/lease policy path.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Use EffectGate.execute as the current authorize callback and retain the F2 executor call afterward.
counterhypotheses.reason: EffectGate.execute already performs the effect and finalizes the journal, creating double-dispatch risk.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Production F2 should delegate the complete real-effect transaction to the canonical EffectGate and treat F2 as correlation/completion consumer rather than a second dispatcher.
counterhypotheses.reason: This preserves one effect authority, current lease lifetime, journal-before-effect ordering and no-blind-replay semantics without inventing a second policy path. It requires adapting the current F2 two-stage port/acceptance shape and proving exact call correlation around the single canonical execution call.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Extend canonical EntityOS authority with an explicit prepare/dispatch/finalize API.
counterhypotheses.reason: Potentially valid only if the canonical source owns the split, preserves all current gate checks and defines lease custody/recovery across the split. This is a semantic authority/API change and must not be invented inside F2.

next_exact_action_for_active_wp105: Do not wire the current two-stage CanonicalEffectAuthorityPort directly to EffectGate.execute. First discriminate the production topology with a deterministic no-real-effect integration harness against the bound API: preferred test = one canonical EffectGate-owned execution call with F2 request/tool/delegation correlation before entry and structured execution/completion correlation after return, proving one EffectJournal.begin, at most one action dispatch, exact effect_id lineage, and UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART no replay. If two-stage control is still required, obtain a canonical EntityOS-owned prepare/dispatch/finalize API including lease custody before implementing it in F2.
